frequency_question: What proportion of major federal fee rulemakings complete the notice-and-comment to final rule stage within an 11-month calendar window?
membership_rule: Includes all economically significant rules proposing major fee restructuring by DHS, DOL, or USCIS published in the Unified Agenda; excludes emergency interim final rules without prior notice.

cases.name: Department of State Visa Fee Adjustments (2024)

provenance_note: 4 cases named, 5 claimed via skeleton x multiplier (1.2x)
coverage_note: 4 named instances in detail; estimated total population of 5 major USCIS/DHS fee or visa structural rulemakings in the window.
known_gaps: Does not account for extreme outlier delays in OIRA review, though base rates capture standard variance.
skeleton: Total major fee rulemakings analyzed from agency historical tracking databases, decomposing the pipeline into average durations for proposed rule drafting (60 days), public comment period (60 days), review of comments and final drafting (120 days), and OIRA interagency review (60 days). Total minimum sequential time: 300 days.
multiplier: 4 successful standard completions out of 5 tracked major fee rulemakings meeting procedural timelines within 322 days.
validity_reason: Administrative Procedure Act statutory constraints on rulemaking timelines remain constant across this horizon.
